raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The Rust frontend answers 404 on `/v1/tokenize` and `/v1/detokenize`, which Python serves through `OpenAIServingTokenize` and `OpenAIServingDetokenize`. A client that counts tokens before sending a prompt, or decodes ids it received, cannot use a Rust-mode server.

## Modifications

Serve `/v1/tokenize` and `/v1/detokenize`, plus the unversioned `/tokenize` and `/detokenize` aliases, from the Rust frontend with Python's request and response shapes:

- `/v1/tokenize` takes `prompt` (a string or a list of strings) or chat `messages`, and `add_special_tokens` (default true). It returns `tokens`, `count` and `max_model_len`. Messages render through the chat template and encode without auto-added specials, as on the chat path.
- `/v1/detokenize` takes `tokens` (a list, or a list of lists) and `skip_special_tokens` (default true), and returns `text`.
- Errors use Python's flat `ErrorResponse` body. A malformed body, or both or neither of `prompt` and `messages`, is a 400 of type `Bad Request`. A rejected input is a 400 `BadRequestError`; other failures are a 500 `InternalServerError`.

How it is wired:

- Encoding runs on the tokenizer pool as a new `RequestKind::Tokenize`, which the pool answers through the request's own sink with a `ResponseItem::TokenIds`; intake does not register it with a detok shard.
- Decoding reuses the detok shards' `RequestKind::Detokenize`, which now carries `skip_special_tokens`. The `/v1/completions` echo path still decodes with it set.
- `max_model_len` is the Python tokenizer's `model_max_length`, or the context length when that is not a 64-bit integer, derived at launch the way `OpenAIServingTokenize` derives it (the `getattr` mirrors that code; the tokenizer is `None` under `skip_tokenizer_init`) and stamped into the Rust `ServerArgs` as `tokenizer_model_max_length`.
- A dropped tokenize or detokenize call (client gone, or `try_join_all` dropping the rest of a list after one failure) releases only its Rust-side state through a new `AbortSource::Local`. It never reached the scheduler, so it queues no scheduler `AbortReq`; otherwise a cancelled list of thousands of prompts would push thousands of aborts ahead of generation requests.
- `ChatRequest` in `openai/chat.rs` becomes `pub(super)` so the tokenize route can render `messages` with the same parser; its PD routing fields are accepted and ignored there.

Differences from Python, on purpose:

- Negative token ids are a 400 here (validated before decoding); Python fails inside the tokenizer with a 500.
- Media in `messages` is rejected, as on the Rust chat route.

This PR is independent of #44533 and #44532: it touches neighbouring lines of `ServerArgs` and `rust_server/config.py` but shares no hunk with either.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model forward or kernel change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the new routes do not sit on the generation path. The only change on it is one extra `bool` on the `Detokenize` message.

## Test plan

- `rust/`: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server`: 335 passed. The one failure, `chunk_event_frame_stays_small`, fails identically on untouched `main` on this aarch64 machine (`ChunkEvent` is 152 bytes there against a 144-byte ceiling) and is unrelated to this change.
  - New: `tokenize_answers_through_the_sink_without_returning_to_intake`, `tokenize_goes_to_the_pool_without_detok_registration`, `tokenize_returns_python_response_shape`, `detokenize_returns_python_response_shape`, `invalid_requests_get_the_flat_python_error`, `token_operations_mint_internal_rids`; `every_abort_source_deregisters_and_stops_the_scheduler` now also covers `AbortSource::Local` pushing no scheduler abort.
- Python: `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_rust_server_dp_ports.py`: 23 passed, including the new `test_tokenizer_model_max_length_matches_python_tokenize` (no tokenizer, no attribute, configured value, HF's `int(1e30)` unset sentinel).
- Lint: isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1 (`check` and `format`), codespell 2.4.1 clean on the touched files.
- Not run here: an end-to-end server. The routes were exercised against a Rust-mode and a Python-mode server with the same small instruct model and matched status and body for string and list prompts with and without `add_special_tokens`, `""`, `[]`, `messages` with and without a system message, the aliases, nested token lists, `skip_special_tokens` true and false, `[[9906], []]`, and the malformed bodies listed above (same `object`, `type` and `code`; the messages differ, serde's text against pydantic's).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
